title: InboundEventV1dot2
description: K-06, the inbound event, v1.2 (T-1296), a minor version. The root is v1's event exactly: it is inbound-event.v1.schema.json (frozen and unchanged; v1.1 is v1's shape too), through allOf, with v1's required list repeated. So every v1 and v1.1 event is a v1.2 event. (v1.1 refers to v1 by a root $ref; v1.2 goes through allOf so that the type generator, which follows a root $ref before it reads this file's own $defs, finds them.) v1.2 adds two things. (1) The named rule scrubbedV1dot2 (inbound-event.rules.mjs): a poll's option words follow the body's scrub, v1.1's reading, before anything is kept, because a vote for an option someone added reads as typed words (arch 07 line 379; S13-24 rule 6), and scrubbed counts what was swapped in them too (arch 02 line 109; arch 10 line 516; RULES 4.5 line 199: 'Never kept at all: full card numbers outside the card box, full Social Security numbers'; CQ-58). (2) Under $defs, the sealed hand-off: the event as the gateway hands it to the handle's actor and as the actor keeps it (sealedEvent), with its words (the body, an email's subject and a poll's option words) taken out and sealed in a box of form version 2 (sealedBox, opened to sealedWords), never kept as a plain field; and the form version 1 box and event the gateway made before v1.2 (sealedBoxV1, sealedWordsV1, sealedEventV1), which are never made again and still open and read as they are (T-243; CQ-58; T-1265's security review). Owner: the architect.

allOf.description: v1's event, frozen and unchanged: its fields, its required list, additionalProperties false and both dependentSchemas. Under v1.2 the body, an email's subject and a poll's option words take the scrub (scrubbedV1dot2), scrubbed counts what was swapped in all three, and the gateway seals all three in one box (sealedEvent).

sealedEvent.title: SealedEvent
sealedEvent.description: The sealed hand-off of v1.2: the event as the gateway hands it to the handle's actor and as the actor keeps it (the inbox stores it whole; T-243, T-244). It is the v1.2 event after the scrub with every word a person typed taken out and sealed in one box under the handle's key: no body, an email reply's email without its subject, a vote's poll without its option words. Every other field is the event's, in the clear, so the actor orders, dedupes and routes on it (arch 02 line 109: 'Before any write it swaps card numbers ... and Social Security numbers for a tag. It writes the sealed event to the handle's actor'; arch 10 line 516: 'private data sealed under a per-person key'; CQ-58). Only the six kinds that go to the handle's actor take this form (README 'Routing'); a delivery receipt has no words and goes to the dispatcher as the event is.

eventId.description: The event's eventId, unchanged: the dedupe key (arch 02 line 109), and with the actor name the box's additional data (sealedBox).

handle.description: The event's handle, unchanged. It names the handle's actor, '<kind>:<address>' (arch 10 line 502: one actor per handle), and the key the box is sealed under (NQ-RT-1's default: the handle's key, made on first sight; T-243).

kind.description: One of the six kinds that go to the handle's actor, in order (README 'Routing'; arch 02 line 113). The receipts (delivered, sent, failed) go to the dispatcher and clock arming, never to the actor, so they never take this form.

receivedAt.description: The event's receivedAt, unchanged: the actor's order (README default 2; arch 02 line 113).

scrubbed.description: The event's counts, unchanged: under v1.2 they take in what the scrub swapped in the option's words too (README 'Named rule (v1.2)'; arch 02 line 109). Counts only, never a word.

attachments.description: The event's attachments, unchanged: ids and media types, never a file's content (02-contracts K-06 and K-02).

poll.description: For a vote or a vote removed, the poll and the option by their ids only, which the actor matches on (K-04 outbox_parts.linq_message_id and linq_option_ids; S13-24 rule 6). The option's words are in the box (sealedWords.optionWords), never here (CQ-58; RULES 4.5 line 199). Null for every other kind.

reaction.description: The event's reaction, unchanged: a tapback's name as the Linq port reports it, such as like, and the id of the message it is on (arch 07 line 391). A name from the port's list (README open gaps), not words a person typed.

edit.description: The event's edit, unchanged: the id of the message edited; the new words are in the box (sealedWords.body) (arch 11 line 584).

status.description: Always null: a delivery receipt never reaches the actor (README 'Routing'; arch 02 line 127).

fromRosie.description: The event's fromRosie, unchanged: Rosie's own reaction starts no turn (arch 07 line 391).

email.description: For an email reply, its reply address and sender check; its subject is in the box (sealedWords.subject), never here (arch 02 line 109). Null for Linq.

sealed.description: The event's words after the scrub, sealed under the handle's key: a box of form version 2 for every kind with words (a text, a photo, an edit, an email reply, a vote and a vote removed), null for a reaction, which has none (T-243; CQ-58). The gateway seals only after the scrub, so what the box holds passes scrubbedV1dot2's reading.

provider.description: An email reaches the actor only as a reply (kind text), so it carries its email, subject sealed; a Linq event carries none (RULES 4.1, 6.1; 02-contracts K-12; README 'Routing').

kind.description: An email reply is kind text (README default 5); the email provider's receipts go to the dispatcher.

email.description: RULES 4.1, 6.1: the reply address and the sender check; the subject is sealed.

kind.description: Where each kind's words are: in the box for every kind that has words, nowhere for a reaction (CQ-58; T-243). A vote names its poll by ids only.

sealed.description: A text's, a caption's, an edit's or an email reply's words, or a vote's option words: sealed, never plain (arch 02 line 109; CQ-58).
A tapback has no words to seal (arch 07 line 391).

poll.description: arch 07 line 379; arch 03 line 187: the poll and the option by id; the words are sealed.

sealedPoll.title: SealedPoll
sealedPoll.description: A vote's poll and option as the actor keeps them: their ids in the clear, which the actor matches against the poll part K-04 holds (outbox_parts.linq_message_id and linq_option_ids; an option id that is none of Rosie's is an option someone added: S13-24 rule 6). It has no optionWords: the option's words are only in the box (sealedWords.optionWords; CQ-58).

sealedEmailReply.title: SealedEmailReply
sealedEmailReply.description: An email reply's own fields as the actor keeps them: the reply address, which picks the booking and its thread (RULES 4.1), and the sender check (RULES 6.1), in the clear. It has no subject: the subject is only in the box (sealedWords.subject; arch 02 line 109; T-243).

sealedBox.title: SealedBox
sealedBox.description: The box v1.2's gateway seals an event's words in, form version 2. The seal is form version 1's, unchanged (T-243; runtime/src/gateway/seal.ts): AES-256-GCM through WebCrypto under the handle's data key (AES-256; K-05 v1.2 handleSealingKey), a fresh random 96-bit IV for each seal and a 128-bit tag; the additional data is the UTF-8 text '<actor name>|<event id>' (actor name '<handle.kind>:<handle.address>'), so a box copied onto another event or handle does not open. What it seals is the UTF-8 of one JSON text, sealedWords: the body, the subject and the option's words. Version 2 differs from version 1 only in that third member (CQ-58). Never logged, put in a span or answered: a key, an opened box.

v.description: The box's form: 2, which opens to sealedWords (body, subject and optionWords). A reader takes a box's words by its form and refuses a form it does not know (README 'The sealed hand-off (v1.2)').

iv.description: The 12-byte IV, in standard base64: 16 characters, no padding (T-243).

ct.description: The cipher text with its 16-byte tag after it, as one standard base64 string, padded (T-243).

sealedWords.title: SealedWords
sealedWords.description: What a box of form version 2 holds once opened: one JSON text with exactly these three members, the event's words after the scrub, each null where the event has none. An opened box with a member missing, another member, or a member of another type is refused, and nothing in it is read (README 'The sealed hand-off (v1.2)'). Each member passes scrubbedV1dot2's reading.

body.description: The event's body after the scrub: a text's words, a photo's caption or an empty string, an edit's new words, an email reply's text (arch 02 line 109). Null for a vote and a vote removed.

subject.description: An email reply's subject after the scrub (arch 02 line 109). Null for Linq.

optionWords.description: A vote's or a vote removed's option words after the scrub: Rosie's option word for word, or the words of an option someone added, read as typed words (arch 07 line 379; S13-24 rule 6; K-02's poll-vote text carries them as its words). Null for every other kind.

sealedBoxV1.title: SealedBoxV1
sealedBoxV1.description: The box the gateway made before v1.2, form version 1 (T-243): the same seal as version 2 (cipher, key, IV, tag and additional data), opened to sealedWordsV1. Never made after v1.2; every one already kept still opens as it is, under the same key and additional data (the card: 'old boxes still opened as they are').

v.description: The box's form: 1, which opens to sealedWordsV1 (body and subject).

iv.description: The 12-byte IV, in standard base64, as in version 2.

ct.description: The cipher text with its tag, in standard base64, as in version 2.

sealedWordsV1.title: SealedWordsV1
sealedWordsV1.description: What a box of form version 1 holds once opened: one JSON text with exactly the body and the subject after the scrub (T-243). It has no option words: an event kept with a version 1 box, or with none, is sealedEventV1, whose vote keeps its option words plain.

sealedEventV1.title: SealedEventV1
sealedEventV1.description: The event as the gateway handed it to the actor before v1.2 (T-243), which an actor may still hold: sealedEvent's fields, but a text's, a photo's, an edit's or an email reply's words in a version 1 box, and a vote's or a vote removed's option words plain in poll.optionWords with no box. Never made after v1.2: the gateway hands over sealedEvent. A reader still reads one as it is: the body and the subject from its version 1 box, a vote's words from its poll.optionWords. Those plain words passed no scrub, so they may hold a card number or a Social Security number (CQ-58); they go with the text's rows and at a person's delete, not with the key (ADR-017 open point 8).

scrubbed.description: The event's counts as v1.1's scrub made them: the body and the subject only (README 'Named rule (v1.1)').

poll.description: For a vote or a vote removed, v1's poll, its option's words plain (T-243 sealed only the body and the subject: CQ-58). Null for every other kind.

email.description: As sealedEvent.email: the subject was in the version 1 box.

sealed.description: A version 1 box for a text, a photo, an edit or an email reply; null for a reaction, a vote and a vote removed, which T-243 did not seal (T-243: only the body and the subject were sealed).

kind.description: Where each kind's words were before v1.2 (T-243): a text's, a caption's, an edit's or an email reply's in a version 1 box; a vote's plain in its poll, with no box.

sealed.description: T-243: the body and an email's subject, sealed.
T-243 sealed nothing for these kinds.

poll.description: arch 07 line 379: v1's poll, the option's words plain.
